title: Affine fibre identifications, geometric reducedness comparison and finiteness
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be any homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $f:X=\operatorname{Spec}B\to T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be its affine scheme morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For $\mathfrak p\in T$ put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A k)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, with structure map induced by $k\to B\otimes_A k$, $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. Consequently, for a geometric fibre over any chosen algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre],
$$X_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\text{ is reduced}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A k)\text{ is geometrically reduced over }k,$$
where reduced is [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and geometrically reduced means reduced after every field extension [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For every ring map $a:A\to A'$, the base-change projection $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A'$ [def-pc-base-change] is identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A A')\to\operatorname{Spec}A'$, induced by $c\mapsto1\otimes c$; the other projection is induced by $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. These identifications require no finiteness assumption. Both $X$ and $T$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and $f$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $A\to B$ is finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], then $f$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Empty source, empty base and empty fibres are allowed.

proof.text: For any $A\to A'$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] to the two $A$-algebras $B$ and $A'$. It identifies $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A A')$. Its projection formulas identify the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with $c\mapsto1\otimes c$ and the projection to $X$ with $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Thus the identification is over the stated base, not merely an abstract scheme isomorphism. The lemma has no finiteness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), tensor product formula and its universal-property proof

proof.text: For $\mathfrak p\in T$, [def-pc-scheme-fibre] defines $X_{\mathfrak p}=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}k$, where $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Take $A'=k$ in the affine pullback lemma. The resulting isomorphism $X_{\mathfrak p}\cong Y:=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A k)$ is over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ because its second projection is induced by $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. This proves the fibre assertion with its precise structure map.

Fix the chosen algebraic closure $\bar k/k$. By [def-weil-geometric-fibre], the geometric fibre is equivalently the base change of $X_{\mathfrak p}$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The isomorphism over $k$ in step 2 induces an isomorphism of this base change with $Y_{\bar k}$: apply the fibre-product universal property to that isomorphism and its inverse; their composites are identities since both projections agree. Isomorphic schemes have isomorphic local rings, so reducedness agrees by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-algebraic-closure-test] to the $k$-scheme $Y$. It gives $Y_{\bar k}$ reduced if and only if $Y$ is reduced after every field extension of $k$, exactly the geometric reducedness asserted in the item. This lemma allows arbitrary $k$, arbitrary chosen algebraic closure, and arbitrary $Y$.

source.place: Tag 035X (lemma-geometrically-reduced), (2) iff (6) in positive characteristic; Tag 020I (lemma-perfect-reduced) and reducedness descent in characteristic zero

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] separately to $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Both are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] then applies to $f$, using quasi-compactness of its source and quasi-separatedness of its target, and gives that $f$ is quasi-compact. Nothing here uses finite generation or finite presentation of $B$ over $A$.

Now suppose $A\to B$ is finitely presented. By [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], choose a presentation $B\cong A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. At every $x\in X$, take the affine neighbourhoods $U=X$ and $V=T$ in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The induced ring map is precisely the given finitely presented map $A\to B$, so $f$ is of finite presentation at $x$ and hence locally of finite presentation. If $X$ is empty this condition is vacuous. The preceding steps require no points of $X$: for $B=0$ all fibre rings are zero and all source schemes empty; for $A=0$ a unital $A$-algebra is zero and there are no primes to test. A zero fibre ring similarly gives an empty reduced geometric fibre. Thus the assertions include empty source, base and fibres.
